newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to up, pork bellies higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent per lb higher while pork bellies were called 0.200 to 1.000 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Steady to higher cash hog indications linked to light hog runs and a firmer tone to some pork products were expected to spark demand in hog futures. Hog runs remain light as farmer concentrate on fieldwork and packers are showing stronger demand after loin prices rebounded by $2.00 per cwt on Tuesday, analysts said.
Interior hog marketings have been running lighter than projected the past couple of days, some sources noted.

Pork bellies were seen rising following a bullishly-interpreted weekly CME out-of-town storage report and expectations that cash belly prices have bottomed. Continued relatively light hog slaughter and a technically stronger chart picture were also cited, they said.

CME reported a net out-movement of 952,000 lbs last week from warehouses outside Chicago which compared with an in-movement of 333,000 lbs last year. Out-of-town stocks are now only slightly above last year and may decline below year-ago as storings were seen light or declining most of May, sources noted.
Delivery concerns were abating as demand for stored product was seen strong going into summer when hog slaughter could slip further than the already-slow pace, they added.
USDA estimated hog slaughter through Tuesday this week at 313,000 head, below 329,000 in the same period a week ago and 339,000 a year ago.
